## Changes since `v0.7.1-beta.3`

### Features

- badge a WSL tab's distribution logo as local: with the logo, a WSL Ubuntu tab looked just like an SSH tab to an Ubuntu host; a WSL tab showing a distribution's logo, reported or picked, now carries a small inverted square with a prompt in its corner, a square so it is not taken for the attention dots beside it, while SSH tabs and glyph icons stay as they were ([c3be0d39](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/c3be0d398aa25a7856422814feebc9b6bd7c3709))
- show a WSL tab's distribution logo: a WSL tab always showed the same orange terminal icon, whichever distribution it ran, while an SSH tab showed its host's logo; the WSL launcher now reports the ID, ID_LIKE and NAME from os-release as it starts the shell (OSC 777 ; tterm-os), the tab keeps the distribution it names and shows its logo, under any icon the user picked for WSL or for the tab, and a restored tab shows it before WSL is up ([3f10e364](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/3f10e3648e8878195cbb2eef773c973a213a7c19))
- restore each terminal tab's content after a restart: a restored tab opened on an empty terminal, so what it had shown before tTerm closed was gone; under General, Startup, Restore terminal content after a restart, off by default, now keeps each terminal's main screen and scrollback down to its cursor, up to 5000 lines with colors but without modes or a full-screen program's screen, saves the terminals that changed every 10 seconds and once more before a quit or a relaunch, and shows it again above the tab's new session under a dim line with when it was saved; turning it off deletes what was saved, importing a session from a backup drops it so the imported tabs never show another tab's content, and the setting syncs with the others ([b6de1341](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b6de134120e2984373ae12b1a09ed90a49127803))
- let the UI save before the app quits: every quit, from the tray, the window, Cmd+Q or the tunnels' confirmation, ended the webview at once, so what it kept only in memory was lost; once the UI says it has something to save, a quit now tells it with app-will-quit and waits up to 1.5 seconds for its answer, a second quit while waiting goes ahead at once, and without anything to save a quit is as immediate as before ([b6bb8fdd](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b6bb8fddf087ac73bc3900fd9dc463e9f0148bef))
- keep each terminal tab's content on disk for the next launch: a restart showed every tab empty, as nothing kept what its terminal had shown; each tab's content can now be saved as a gzip file under scrollback/ in the config folder, owner-only on Unix and outside the database so backups and sync never carry it, read back for the tabs of the restored session, and deleted once its tab is no longer in the saved session or the session is cleared ([42ffbb4f](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/42ffbb4f18079fbb399b0eec979478b31fb5b57c))

### Fixes

- end a bracketed paste a Ctrl+C cuts short: a Ctrl+C stops what is still queued of a paste, and with it the marker that ends a bracketed paste, so the program kept taking whatever was typed next for more of the paste; the end marker is now written before the Ctrl+C, after the unread input of a Windows console is discarded so that the discard does not drop it as well ([6daf85b8](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/6daf85b813f65ee6ae4f4b97cfcd0cca9f8063e9))

### Performance

- write a bracketed paste at once instead of pacing it: a large paste into Claude Code took a second or more to show, since a paste was written only as fast as the program answered it with output, and a program that turned on bracketed paste, as Claude Code and zsh do, holds the whole paste silently until its end, so each doubling of the window waited out a 100 ms stall; a paste starting with the bracketed paste marker is now written straight away, while one without it is still paced so that a Ctrl+C can stop it ([dd1e15d7](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/dd1e15d772ef92af16d20a12f539261d7d2fefbe))
- send terminal output that follows a pause at once: every read opened an 8 ms batching window before it went to the webview, so the echo of each keystroke waited out the window, and on Windows, whose timer ticks about every 15.6 ms, the wait came to nearly 19 ms; output arriving a full window after the last batch now goes out immediately, while output inside a burst still coalesces, in a window that ends one interval after the previous batch ([34052045](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/34052045321a4676ae8386be87d5b0be36554270))

### UI and usability

- shorten the restored-content line back to a short dim mark: the line across the whole terminal drew the eye away from the new session, and wrapped once the window narrowed; it is again a short dash on each side of the text, keeping the 24-hour time, which now leads with the year when the content was saved in another year ([5576dc71](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/5576dc71cdcce3ae500ef15587cf785ce0b6b2ae))
- draw the restored-content line across the terminal with a 24-hour time: the line under a tab's restored content was a short dash pair around the text, with the time in the system's 12-hour form; it now runs the full width of the terminal with the text in its middle, wide characters counted as two cells, and the time reads like 10-25 14:03; the content is written once the terminal has settled on its size, just before its session starts, so the line matches the terminal's width ([b8ffe664](https://github.com/330079598/tTerm/commit/b8ffe6648f01ebbfa5bc001af963b23da75d0242))
